text: Did the patient start any new medication in the weeks before the itch started?

detail.problem: Encoded as (snomed_concept "New medication commenced" "finding"), checked for, positive in the medication rule and negated in the jaundice rule. The temporal relation 'in the weeks before the itch started' (medication onset relative to itch onset) is not representable in the language (onset can only be compared with time_ago, not with another finding's onset), so its omission is acceptable.

parts_missing: The time window 'in the weeks before the itch started' is not encoded. New medication commenced has no onset or recency constraint, so a medication started years ago, or after the itch began, also counts if recorded.
detail.problem: The language cannot express onset relative to another finding. It could approximate the window with (< (onset (clinical_finding New medication commenced)) (time_ago N weeks)) in the due_to, but the rule does not do this.

text: Jaundice is gated on (no Severe dry skin) and (no New medication commenced), as the flowchart orders the branches. A patient with itch and yellow skin/eyes who also has very dry skin, or recently started a medication, never gets probable jaundice. Jaundice is the most serious cause on the page (-> page 94), and a drug can itself cause cholestatic jaundice. The rule is faithful to the page's layout, but the sequential gating suppresses a high-value diagnosis. A clinician should confirm whether yellow skin/eyes should override the earlier branches.
